attribution.note: Marcus's own analytical sentence in his own post. He hedges only the attribution to OpenAI.

semantics.note: Keeps the 'if I recall correctly' hedge on OpenAI's role, the concession that the milestone matters, and the departure-from-cognitive-criteria comparison. It is a conceptual comparison with some evaluative colour.

contract.note: The plain reading is ordinary and fair: compare what earlier definitions required with what an economic-share criterion requires. It rightly keeps the uncertain OpenAI attribution apart from the comparison.

evidence.note: Legg and Hutter (2007) define intelligence as achieving goals across a wide range of environments, with adaptation built in. This dates well before publication and matches the 'cognitive criteria' Marcus says the field discussed.

reviews.rationale: Earlier field definitions (e1) stress breadth and adaptation across environments. As stated, an 80%-of-work criterion does not separately require that generality: Marcus's example of separate domain-specific systems shows this. The support condition is met. Whether OpenAI actually used the 80% figure is unverified, but he hedged it and it is not scored.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: 'Ever since' refers back to OpenAI's February 2023 definition, so 'since early 2023' is faithful. 'A lot' is vague but firm.

contract.note: Reading 'mission creep' as substantial post-Feb-2023 shifts toward economic or permissive criteria is the ordinary reading. Separating real changes from long-standing rival definitions is reasonable.

evidence.note: OpenAI's own Feb 2023 cognitive framing. It sets the baseline only.

Oct 2023 essay arguing current models already count as AGI. It is one in-period example of a more permissive threshold, though advocacy rather than an actor changing its own definition. The source-type label is loose.
Dates OpenAI's economic charter definition to 2018, before the period. That weakens its use as an example of post-2023 creep.

reviews.rationale: The packet gives one clear in-period example (Noema, e2). The main economic definition (e3) predates the period, and the $100B profit report was not readable here. The contract asks for multiple substantial in-period changes, and the record is not broad enough to show continuity either. Not settled.

attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence. He relays The Information's reporting but endorses the characterisation that OpenAI shifted.

semantics.note: Keeps 'apparently', 'according to The Information' and 'considering'. 'Apparently' is an evidential qualifier, not a probability hedge, and the core claim about what was reported is firm and checkable.

contract.note: Scoring the existence and content of the reporting on a profit-generation AGI criterion is a fair reading of his qualified wording. Not requiring replacement of OpenAI's public definition is also fair.

evidence.note: Business Insider (Dec 26, 2024) attributes to The Information a 2023 Microsoft–OpenAI agreement defining AGI as a system able to generate $100B in profits. It matches the amount and measure. 'Agreed' is stronger than Marcus's 'considering'.

reviews.rationale: Reputable reporting at the time confirms The Information described a $100B profit-based AGI criterion between Microsoft and OpenAI. The only mismatch is 'considering' versus 'agreed', and that understates the case rather than contradicting it. The contradiction condition (different amount, different measure, or a correction) is not met.

attribution.note: Marcus's own prediction in his own post.

semantics.note: 'We can expect' is an unqualified expectation, so it is a scoreable forecast with a 2025 horizon. 'That' refers to the mission creep just described.

contract.note: Requiring multiple substantial new shifts of the kinds he described during 2025 is a fair plain reading. It is right to separate verification procedures and impact measures from definitions.

evidence.note: Nadella (Feb 2025) treats 10% world growth as the real benchmark and dismisses AGI milestone claims. This is partial economic reframing, not a formal new definition.
Altman (Aug 2025) calls AGI 'not a super useful term', which fits avoiding a definition. The same report says his own definition still required continuous learning, which weakens it.
Oct 2025 company disclosure changes who verifies AGI, not the threshold. It does not show definitions weakening.

reviews.rationale: The 2025 horizon has passed. The packet has two partial, qualified examples (Nadella's economic benchmark, Altman distancing himself from the term) and one item about procedure only. That falls short of clearly showing 'a lot more' substantial shifts, and nothing shows definitions stayed stable. The available evidence does not settle it.
